title.narrative: Output 3.1. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement a new generation of gender-responsive national employment policies, including for youth

description.narrative:
1. The Ministry of Labour, Employment and Social Security (MOLESS) developed a Model Employment Strategy aligned with the National Employment Policy (2014), the Local Governance Act and the Nepal Constitution (Provision 33). The strategy considers agriculture, manufacturing, construction, information and communication technology, education, health, tourism and renewable energy as sectors with special employment potential for Nepal. The strategy focuses in addressing employment challenges as a way forward to economic growth, including school-to-work transition, COVID-19 induced job losses and foreign labour migration.
The strategy recognises the primary role of local governments to achieve economic growth. MOLESS therefore circulated a directive to the 753 Municipal Governments of the country instructing the development of local policies based on the Model Strategy.
2. MOLESS strengthened the mechanisms to monitor the implementation of the Prime Minister's Employment Programme (PMEP) by implementing a Project Cycle Management (PCM) training that reached 1,550 staff from Employment Service Centres in all 753 Municipalities of Nepal. 1. The ILO supported the consultation with Association of Municipalities, supported the Ministry in bringing together the WB and other line ministries while developing the Strategy. A senior Labour Market Economist was also recruited to prepare the draft strategy for the MOLESS.
2. ILO in collaboration with MOLESS organised the one –day orientation. An local organisation with expertise on PCM training was outsourced by the ILO to organise this training in coordination with the Municipalities.
Activities were carried out with support from the Government of the United Kingdom.
